Evidence reels

Watch a place come back.

An evidence reel is a patch of ground photographed over time, so you can see what an act of kindness does to it. Three kinds of kindness, three kinds of experiment: leave a place alone, enhance it, or simply observe and record what is already there. This is the most honest proof we have that small human care changes what lives around us.

Leave alone Enhance Observe
Nature Counts · this year

New ground, watched from the start.

This year we are opening reels on new sites and new patches of wildness across the network: places we have not measured before, recorded from their very first frame so the baseline is honest. Some we will enhance, some we will simply leave alone, and all of them we will count.

If you have a place, that first photograph is the most valuable one you will ever take of it, because everything after is measured against it. Start now, even before anything has changed.

Open a reel on your place →

Restoration is slower and messier than a tidy before-and-after suggests. A left-alone patch can look worse before it looks better, more nettles before more butterflies. We show the awkward middle too, because that is where the truth is.
